book.title: The Telegraph All New Toughie Crossword, book 1

clue.text: Yells about editor and female being close associates

indicators.note: the word for the yells goes around the next pieces, surrounding them on both sides

parts.note: bellows are loud shouts
ED is the usual short form of editor
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: Shouting at the editor and some woman somehow turns them into close friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' sends the shouting word around the others, which split it after its first letter rather than sitting at one end.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedfellows, literally people sharing a bed, is the idiom for allies or people closely linked.

clue.text: Not a person immune from criticism, but sounds like it

definitions.text: Not a person immune from criticism

indicators.note: says the preceding word, when spoken, has the same sound as the solution

parts.note: the conjunction but, spoken, matches a word for the target of jokes

explanation.surface: Not someone safe from criticism, yet appearing to be so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'But' looks like a plain conjunction; it is the word to be heard.
explanation.definitionFit: The butt of jokes or criticism is the person they are aimed at, the opposite of someone immune.

clue.text: Occupant of study, one with a certain kind of faith

indicators.note: with means alongside, so the pieces either side are simply placed next to each other

parts.note: a den is a small private room or study
the Roman numeral for one
Zen is a school of Buddhism

explanation.surface: Whoever sits in the study turns out to be a person of a particular religion.
explanation.definitionFit: A denizen is an inhabitant or resident of a place, so an occupant.

clue.text: Funny pieces of Internet meant to provide this?

definitions.text: Funny pieces of Internet meant to provide this?

indicators.note: funny means odd or peculiar, so the letters that follow are put into a strange new order

parts.note: the two words taken letter for letter as raw material

explanation.surface: Amusing bits of the web exist to give us this.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: amusing online clips are there to give amusement.
explanation.definitionFit: Funny clips posted online are meant to amuse, and amusement is what the solution names.

clue.text: Drink brave person's taken outside one club

indicators.note: the brave person has been placed on the outside, so that word wraps around the rest

parts.note: a lion is a byword for a brave person
the Roman numeral for one
a bat is a club used in cricket or baseball

explanation.surface: A courageous drinker downs a glass outside a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for has: the lion has taken I and BAT inside, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A libation is an alcoholic drink, originally wine poured out as an offering to a god.

clue.text: Revolver once used for torture

definitions.meaning: first meaning: anything that turns on an axle

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the thing, not a noun
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the device on which victims were broken in past centuries

explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolver' suggests a gun used to threaten someone; it is just a thing that turns. Breaking on the wheel was a medieval punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheel rotates on its axle, and the breaking wheel was a historical instrument of torture and execution.

clue.text: Left amateur, originally, in charge — not professional

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for left

indicators.note: originally points to the start of the word before it, so only its opening letter is wanted

parts.note: the first letter of amateur
IC is the usual abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: Someone who quit as an amateur, once in charge, is not a professional.
explanation.walkthrough: LAIC means lay: of the laity rather than the clergy, the professional churchmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Laic is a formal word for lay, and lay people are those outside a profession, especially the clergy.

clue.text: Very absorbed in waltz, say? Go on!

indicators.note: something absorbed in another is soaked up inside it, so that piece sits within the next

parts.note: a waltz is an example of a dance, so a dance
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: Someone very caught up in the waltz is urged to keep going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks the waltz as just one example of a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: To advance is to move forward or proceed, which is to go on.

clue.text: Competitor steady — extremely tense inside

indicators.note: inside says the selected letters go within the word for steady

parts.note: constant means steady and unchanging

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of a word, its first and last letters only

parts.note: the first and last letters of tense

explanation.surface: A contestant stays steady though very tense inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely tense' reads as nerves; it means only the two outer letters of tense.
explanation.definitionFit: A contestant is someone who takes part in a contest or competition.

clue.text: European accepted in Indian's home, in principle

indicators.note: something accepted in a place is taken inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a tepee or wigwam, the traditional home of a Native American, is a kind of tent
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A European has been taken into a Native American dwelling, at least in theory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In principle' reads as a stock phrase, but 'in' is only the link and 'principle' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a belief or doctrine held as true, which is a principle.

clue.text: Be calm, though inwardly a tormented genius

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: inwardly says the word before it sits inside another, here the word for calm

parts.note: even, as in an even temper, means calm
tho is an informal spelling of though

explanation.surface: Advice to keep calm, even though a tortured genius is raging inside you.
explanation.walkthrough: BE then E(THO)VEN. The composer went deaf and was famously troubled, hence 'tormented genius'.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven is the classic example of a tortured artist: a musical genius plagued by deafness, illness and a stormy temper.

clue.text: Hard speech by South African sportsman about English hero

indicators.note: by means next to, so these pieces are set side by side in order

parts.note: H stands for hard, as on pencils
an oration is a formal speech
Ernie Els, the South African golfer
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: A South African sportsman gives a tough speech about an English hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like a container signal but simply gives ON. Nelson was the admiral killed winning at Trafalgar.
explanation.definitionFit: Admiral Lord Nelson, victor at Trafalgar in 1805, is one of Britain's greatest national heroes.

clue.text: Tough law-and-order policy having no margin of error

definitions.meaning: first meaning: strict policing that punishes every minor offence
second meaning: in engineering, a tolerance is the allowed deviation, so allowing none

explanation.surface: A hard-line policing policy that leaves no room for mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: The engineering sense of tolerance, the permitted variation in a measurement, gives the second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a strict policing approach and, literally, an allowed variation of nothing at all.

clue.text: Impressive displays as visual aids

definitions.meaning: first meaning: grand shows or sights
second meaning: glasses that help you see

explanation.walkthrough: 'Visual aids' suggests a teacher's charts or slides, but here they are a pair of glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectacle is a striking public show, and spectacles in the plural are eyeglasses.

clue.text: Figure in plane from military HQ

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a flat five-sided shape in geometry
second meaning: the US Department of Defense building in Virginia

explanation.surface: Some figure seen in an aircraft that came from army headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plane' suggests an aircraft, but here it is the flat surface of plane geometry.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-sided polygon shares its name with the five-sided US defence headquarters building.

clue.text: Attending trial to be a witness

parts.note: attending an event is being at it
a trial is a test

explanation.surface: Someone goes to a court trial in order to give evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: The courtroom picture makes 'trial' look legal; it is simply a test.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to bear witness, declaring formally that something is true.

clue.text: Unusually rare slip can result in retaliation

indicators.note: unusually means not in the normal way, so the letters are taken in an abnormal order

parts.note: the letters of these two words, used as raw material

explanation.surface: An uncommon mistake may provoke someone to strike back.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprisal is an act of retaliation, punishing someone in return for an injury.

clue.text: Shrewd, taking rook in restricted opening

indicators.note: taking something in means absorbing it, so one piece is placed inside the word for shrewd
completes the phrase taking ... in, meaning admitting a letter within

parts.note: canny means shrewd, especially with money
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: A clever chess player captures a rook within a cramped opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' sounds like chess here, but it means a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A cranny is a small narrow gap or crevice, as in nooks and crannies.

clue.text: Pass for Cockney in English Town

indicators.note: Cockney speakers famously drop the h at the start of words, so the opening letter goes

parts.note: to pass something is to hand it over

explanation.surface: A Cockney passing through an English town.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the working-class London accent, which drops H. Andover is a market town in Hampshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Andover is a town in Hampshire, in southern England.

clue.text: Under obligation to live with husband in past

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
H is the abbreviation for husband
olden means of the past, as in the olden days

explanation.surface: In the past, a woman was obliged to live with her husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Being beholden means owing someone a debt or favour, so obliged to them.

clue.text: Extremely blunt American statesman given little time

parts.note: John Foster Dulles, US Secretary of State in the 1950s
T is the abbreviation for time, little meaning short

explanation.surface: A very outspoken American politician is allowed only a brief slot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blunt' suggests outspoken; it means not sharp, and 'extremely' makes it a superlative.
explanation.definitionFit: Dullest is the superlative of dull, meaning least sharp, so most blunt.

clue.text: English poet some German drew marvellously

indicators.note: some means only a part, so the answer is a run of letters inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across these words, from the end of the first to the middle of the last

explanation.surface: An English poet was sketched brilliantly by a German.
explanation.walkthrough: GermAN DREW MARVELLously: the hidden name runs through the end of three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrew Marvell was a seventeenth-century English poet, author of To His Coy Mistress.

clue.text: Joint arrangement that covers a head of the church

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a corner joint where two bevelled edges meet

definitions.text: that covers a head of the church
definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the thing, not a noun
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the tall pointed headdress of a bishop

explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint arrangement' sounds like a shared plan; it is carpentry. 'A head of the church' is a bishop's head, literally.
explanation.definitionFit: In carpentry two angled ends meet at a mitred corner, and a bishop's ceremonial hat has the same name.

clue.text: Builder of small home or large church

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a tiny bird that builds a nest

definitions.note: elliptical: read as builder of a large church
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the architect of St Paul's Cathedral in London

explanation.walkthrough: 'Builder of' serves both halves: one small nest-building bird, and Sir Christopher Wren, who designed St Paul's Cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiny bird builds a small nest, and the architect Christopher Wren designed St Paul's Cathedral.

clue.text: Art patron dressed in jeans is upwardly mobile

indicators.note: someone dressed in clothes is wrapped by them, so one piece sits inside the clothing word

parts.note: Levi's is a well-known brand of jeans
Henry Tate, sugar magnate, founded the Tate Gallery in London

explanation.surface: A wealthy art lover in casual jeans is climbing the social ladder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upwardly mobile' suggests social climbing; the definition means it literally, rising into the air.
explanation.definitionFit: To levitate is to rise and float in the air, which is literally moving upwards.

clue.text: Fight, in practice, holding English weapon

indicators.note: holding means clasping something within, so the word for practice fighting surrounds another piece

parts.note: boxers spar when they fight for practice
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Two fighters train together while one holds an English weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A spear is a long pole with a pointed tip, used as a weapon for thrusting or throwing.

clue.text: Use the Internet as one enslaved, say

indicators.note: say asks for the word to be spoken, keeping its sound but not its spelling

parts.note: a serf was a feudal labourer bound to the land, effectively enslaved

explanation.surface: Browsing the web like a slave chained to the screen.
explanation.definitionFit: To surf the internet is to browse from page to page, a sense borrowed from riding waves.

clue.text: Leader in war, famous Duke

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so only the opening letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: the first letter of war
Duke Ellington, the famous American jazz bandleader

explanation.surface: A tribute to a great wartime commander who was also a famous duke.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the Duke of Wellington, victor at Waterloo, while 'famous Duke' in the wordplay is the jazzman Ellington.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Wellesley, Duke of Wellington, led the British army against Napoleon and is the best-known duke in history.
